subject: Clarify: cloud provider coverage + subservice evidence handoff
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: provider coverage + subservice evidence handoff

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. We're wrapping up Acme Health's vendor diligence for an upcoming pilot and need a concise set of confirmations from Redwood around subservice coverage. Two asks: 

1) Can Redwood confirm which operational controls in your SOC 2 Type II (or an addendum) explicitly cover customer-managed key custody, backups, and tenant isolation when running on CloudVendor's platform? We received CloudVendor's SOC 2 but need a mapping that shows where responsibilities are shared vs. fully covered.

2) If there are gaps, would Redwood accept CloudVendor's attestation addendum (their supplemental coverage letter) as evidence, or do you require Redwood-signed bridge-letter-style wording?

Attachments: Acme_SIG_Q3_2026.xlsx (our questionnaire with line items you can mark), and we pasted a short checklist in the sheet.

Goal: we'd like a short written response (1–2 pages) plus a matrix filled into the attached sheet by EOD Thu 12/3 if possible — that will keep us on our procurement timeline. Let me know if you need CloudVendor contacts; they told us they’ll respond to vendor requests.

Thanks —
Sara
Sara Lin
Senior Information Security Manager
Acme Health
(sara.lin@acmehealth.com)

---
Note: original asks reference CloudVendor SOC artifact attached for context.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: provider coverage + subservice evidence handoff

Sara —

Thanks for the clear ask and for attaching the SIG sheet. Looping in Marissa (security/compliance lead) and Naomi (ops manager) to coordinate the evidence. High level answers up front: 

- Redwood's SOC 2 Type II covers our control implementation for access, change management, and encryption-at-rest for workloads we manage. Where we rely on CloudVendor for physical infrastructure or managed KMS services, responsibility is shared — we will map those controls to CloudVendor's SOC statements.
- We can accept CloudVendor's supplemental attestation (their "attestation addendum") as long as it explicitly states the control owner and timeframe that aligns with our SOC audit period. If there are control gaps (e.g., backup snapshots stored in a vendor-managed vault that CloudVendor doesn't claim coverage for), we'll provide Redwood-specific compensating evidence.

Action plan: Marissa will fill the SIG matrix and annotate which rows are fully covered by Redwood, which are covered by CloudVendor (with SOC reference), and which need supplemental Redwood evidence. We'll return a completed matrix and a short cover memo by 2026-12-03 EOD PT. If CloudVendor needs to be contacted directly, we will cc them and request their attestation addendum with exact wording.

Marissa / Naomi — can you confirm on timing?

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Head of Field Security (GTMs)
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, Sara Lin <sara.lin@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: provider coverage + subservice evidence handoff

Thanks — quick update. Naomi and I pulled the initial mapping and added comments in redwood-subservice-resp-matrix-20261202.xlsx (attached). High-level notes below: 

- KMS/key custody: CloudVendor's SOC 2 (section A3) states they manage the KMS service; they do not assert customer key custody for BYOK models. For BYOK, Redwood performs envelope encryption and manages KEKs in our control plane; we can provide configuration screenshots + key rotation logs as evidence.

- Backups & snapshots: CloudVendor asserts physical and snapshot storage controls but excludes snapshot immutability guarantees in multi-tenant snapshots. Redwood maintains encrypted snapshot replication and can provide an attestation describing encryption-in-transit and at-rest; if Acme needs immutability guarantees we should note that as an uncovered item and discuss product-level mitigations.

- Tenant isolation/network segmentation: covered jointly — CloudVendor provides network hypervisor isolation (their SOC mapping in the attached PDF points to CC6), Redwood operates tenant-level VPCs and uses strict routing policies. We can provide VPC configs and recent network segmentation test artifacts.

Next steps/timing: 
- Today (12/02): Marissa to upload the annotated matrix and 1–page cover memo to the Drive link.
- Tomorrow (12/03) by 3pm PT: provide the completed matrix to Acme + proposed wording for an attestation addendum we can request from CloudVendor if needed.

Sara — I'm happy to coordinate a short call with CloudVendor SOC if you want them on the thread; we can schedule for 12/03 afternoon PT.

–Marissa

Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: redwood-subservice-resp-matrix-20261202.xlsx

From: CloudVendor SOC <soc@cloudvendor.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 15:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: provider coverage + subservice evidence handoff

Hi Marissa / Karthik / Sara —

This is the CloudVendor SOC team. Per your request, we've attached a short coverage summary (CloudVendor_SOC2_Summary_2025.pdf) and can provide an attestation addendum that clarifies which encryptions and snapshot controls are in scope for our report period (Jan–Dec 2025). A couple of notes: 

- Our SOC voice does not extend to customer-managed application keys (BYOK) unless the customer uses CloudVendor KMS managed keys. We can add explicit line-item language in our addendum to state that CloudVendor KMS provides key wrapping and storage for managed keys.
- For multi-tenant snapshot immutability, our standard report covers physical storage controls and encryption, but we cannot assert immutability for tenant-level snapshot copies without a product change or separate escrow arrangement.

If you provide the proposed attestation wording, we can sign and return it by EOD 12/04. For scheduling, we have open slots for a 30-minute call on 12/03 2:00–3:00pm PT.

Regards,
CloudVendor SOC Team
soc@cloudvendor.com

Attachment: CloudVendor_SOC2_Summary_2025.pdf
